title: Bone density scan (DEXA scan) — How it is performed
claims: A bone density scan compares bone density with that expected for a young healthy adult; the difference is expressed as a standard deviation score, and the T score compares the measurement with a young healthy adult.
The World Health Organization classifies T scores as: above -1 SD normal; between -1 and -2.5 SD mildly reduced bone mineral density; at or below -2.5 SD osteoporosis.
The scan usually takes 10 to 20 minutes, and the person can go home afterwards.
A Z score compares bone density with someone of the same age; Z scores are usually used for children and people under 30 who are still growing.
